review.tagline: Inference framework for 1.58-bit ternary LLMs on CPU and GPU
review.summary: bitnet.cpp is Microsoft's llama.cpp-based inference framework with optimized I2_S, TL1 and TL2 kernels for ternary BitNet b1.58 models on x86 and ARM CPUs, plus a GPU kernel. It runs GGUF models through Python scripts for setup, chat and benchmarking. The README reports 1.37x to 6.17x CPU speedups over full-precision baselines.
review.audience: Engineers running or benchmarking 1-bit LLMs on CPUs or edge devices
strengths: Reports 2.37x-6.17x speedups on x86 and 1.37x-5.07x on ARM versus full precision
Runs a 100B BitNet b1.58 model on one CPU at 5-7 tokens per second (per README)
Supports official 2B-4T and embedding models plus Falcon3, Falcon-E and Llama3-8B ternary variants
Includes an end-to-end benchmark script and a dummy-model generator
weaknesses: Only ternary 1-bit models are supported; ordinary GGUF models are out of scope
No HTTP server or OpenAI-compatible API described; usage is via run_inference.py CLI
Kernel support is uneven across models; embedding models have no ARM support
Build needs clang>=18, cmake>=3.22 and Python>=3.10; no Docker or release builds
needs: Needs python>=3.10, cmake>=3.22, clang>=18, conda, huggingface-cli
Models: BitNet-b1.58-2B-4T, BitNet-embedding-0.6B, BitNet-embedding-270M, bitnet_b1_58-large, bitnet_b1_58-3B
